title: Member Services Desk Basis: Rewriting the Particulars of a Custom Application and Field Services Plan
content:
Enrolled acres on a Custom Application and Field Services plan are rewritten on the member's own statement of what they are farming. Raising them is taken freely while the plan's acre ceiling allows it, while lowering them below the acres already worked is refused outright.

The last day of the service window may be moved out only within the programme's window length, and moving it further is a fresh plan rather than an amendment. The home field is the member's own fact and is rewritten on their word. A prescription or a licence verification is recorded only from the document itself, never from what the member or the applicator says about it.

A plan is updated only while it stands in applied, active or weather hold, since a completed or cancelled plan is closed to change. The standing is read against the plan the amendment concerns, identified by its plan number, and it is read before the amendment is recorded.

## Where each particular comes from

| Particular | What it is rewritten on | Limit on the rewrite |
|---|---|---|
| Enrolled acres | the member's own statement of the acres they are farming | raised freely up to the plan's acre ceiling; never lowered below the acres already worked |
| Last day of the service window | the amendment requested | moved out only within the programme's window length |
| The home field the plan is written around | the member's own word | none stated |
| Whether a current prescription is on file | the prescription document | never recorded on what the member or the applicator says |
| Whether the applicator licence is verified | the licence record | never recorded on what the member or the applicator says |

## Points of judgement on hypothetical figures

*A plan enrolled at 900 acres on a programme whose acre ceiling is 4000 acres, with 260 acres already worked.* Raising the enrolment to 1400 acres is taken, the figure being inside the ceiling and the basis being the member's own statement of what they farm. Lowering it to 200 acres is refused outright, because 200 is below the 260 acres already worked. Lowering it to 400 acres sits above the acres already worked and is not caught by that refusal.

*A window moved beyond the programme's length.* Where the last day asked for would put the window past the programme's window length, that is a fresh plan rather than an amendment to this one.
